pairs.evidence: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts:77 The candidate's open file is cut at 64k characters here and again at 4k characters in the assembler (pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py:99), and the model is never told. The system prompt tells it to 'ground yourself in the candidate's current file', so a partial file reaches the model presented as complete, which breaks the rule that truncation must name what it dropped.

techniques.evidence: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts:77 Silent truncation of an elastic context section, with no notice of how much was dropped. pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/app-master/spec-vintage.ts:52 Whether a composed App-master spec (which carries the persona's system-prompt draft) is stale is decided by comparing timestamps (intake updatedAt vs composedAt), not a digest of what shaped the spec. Any dialog turn that bumps updatedAt without changing the brief flags the spec stale and pushes the requestor into a paid recompose. The 2s grace window is the 'compare less' patch the fingerprinting technique warns about.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/app-master/spec-vintage.ts:52 The staleness gate compares timestamps, not a content digest of the inputs that shaped the composed prompt. Line 8 says every dialog turn stamps updatedAt, and line 25's grace window exists only to hide false positives.
app/_lib/agent-hire/transform-run.ts:144 The agent-fit runner gives the Python assembler typed inputs (job, connector catalog, lang), not prompt text it has rendered itself.

app/_lib/agent-hire/bridge-client.ts:205 The connector vocabulary that reaches the spec-drafting prompt comes from Personas' live catalog. The built-in fallback list is labelled source: 'builtin', so it is never presented as the registry's list.

pairs.registryProposal: fingerprinting-and-cache-keys could say explicitly that a timestamp/updatedAt comparison is not a fingerprint: it is the most common substitute and fails in exactly the 'unchanged sessions keep flagging as stale' way.
